claims.text: A hybrid machine-learning-potential and thermodynamic-integration framework can accurately predict melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid framework can be applied across vast HEA compositional spaces.
A sparse set of DFT energies, forces, and stresses for representative configurations is sufficient to train the proposed HEA potential.
The machine-learning potential captures the complex many-body interactions and local disorder of HEAs.
Machine-learning potentials can provide near-DFT accuracy at lower computational cost for high-temperature HEA thermodynamics.
MLP-aided thermodynamic integration enables simulation of high-temperature properties in HEAs.
Thermodynamic integration along a reversible solid-to-liquid path computes the free-energy difference between the phases.
Melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity can be derived from the calculated free energies using the Clausius-Clapeyron relation and fluctuation formulas.
Standard DFT is too computationally expensive for the extensive sampling required by thermodynamic integration in large, disordered HEAs.
Empirical potentials often fail to capture the correct bonding physics in multicomponent HEAs.
CALPHAD requires extensive experimental parameterization data that are sparse for high-melting-point HEAs.
The proposed calculations should cover 0.5 to 1.5 times the melting temperature at 1 atm.
The target compositional domain consists of 5–10 principal elements in near-equiatomic ratios.
Simulation cells containing more than 1000 atoms are needed to capture long-range correlations.
The method is valid for substitutional solid-solution HEAs with moderate to high configurational entropy.
The method may fail for strong chemical ordering, intermetallic formation, extreme compositional asymmetry, or configurations outside the MLP training domain.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality and diversity of the DFT training data.
MLP extrapolation, finite-size effects, and convergence of the thermodynamic-integration path are important sources of uncertainty.
The framework will predict melting temperature within ±50 K, entropy of fusion within ±10%, and heat capacity within ±5% of experiment.
The framework will screen thousands of HEA compositions in days rather than years.

contradictions.description: TaVCrW is given as an example target alloy, but it contains four principal elements, whereas the stated compositional domain requires 5–10 principal elements.
